mainTopic: A man left his property to his grandmother and then 'to my heirs.' Does his late daughter's husband inherit, and what is the rule of ראוי versus מוחזק for a husband and a בכור?
overview: A man wrote: 'My property goes to my grandmother, and after her to my heirs.' His married daughter died before the grandmother. When the grandmother died, the daughter's husband claimed the property as his wife's heir. רב הונא says 'my heirs' includes the heirs of my heirs, so the husband wins. רב ענן says it does not, so the husband loses. A ruling from ארץ ישראל follows רב ענן's result but gives a different reason. The property was only ראוי (due to come) to the wife, and a husband does not inherit ראוי the way he inherits מוחזק (what she actually held). רבי אלעזר defends רב הונא: saying 'after you' is like saying 'from now,' so the wife already owned it. רבה backs the ארץ ישראל view, because the grandmother could have sold the property. רב פפא rules that a husband and a בכור take only from מוחזק, and a בכור gets no double share of a loan.

steps.title: The case: property to the grandmother, then to 'my heirs'
steps.stepSummary: A man left his property to his grandmother and after her to his heirs. His married daughter died before the grandmother. After the grandmother died, the daughter's husband claimed the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'My property to my grandmother, and after her to my heirs.' He had a married daughter. She died while her husband and the grandmother were still alive. After the grandmother died, the husband came and claimed the property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is laying out a real-life case. It sets up the argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter would have been her father's heir. A husband normally inherits his wife. So the husband argues: my wife was his heir, and I am her heir, so the property should come to me.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the timing. The daughter died BEFORE the grandmother, so the property never actually reached the daughter while she was alive.

phrases.english: "My property to my grandmother,
and after her, to my heirs."
He had a daughter who was married,
she died in her husband's lifetime
and in the grandmother's lifetime.
After the grandmother died,
the husband came and was claiming.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Presents the case. The question is whether the husband of the predeceased daughter inherits. The following steps (2-11) answer it.

steps.title: רב הונא: 'my heirs' includes the heirs of my heirs
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reads 'to my heirs' as including their heirs too. So the husband, as heir of the daughter, can collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: 'To my heirs' means even to the heirs of my heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the first ruling. He reads the man's words broadly, so the husband wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fight is over the meaning of the word 'heirs.' רב הונא says it reaches down the chain. The daughter was an heir, and her husband is her heir, so he qualifies.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who rules in the husband's favor here

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
"To my heirs" means even to the heirs of my heirs.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'My heirs' includes heirs of heirs, so the husband inherits.

steps.title: רב ענן: 'my heirs' means only my own heirs
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן reads 'to my heirs' narrowly: only the man's direct heirs, not their heirs. So the husband gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said: 'To my heirs' means only my heirs, not the heirs of my heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן disagrees with רב הונא. He reads the words narrowly, so the husband loses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the question is about the wording. רב ענן says the man meant only the people who are his own heirs at that time. A husband who inherits from one of those heirs is one step too far.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who rules against the husband

phrases.english: And Rav Anan said:
"To my heirs" means not to the heirs of my heirs.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'My heirs' excludes heirs of heirs, so the husband does not inherit.

steps.title: Ruling from ארץ ישראל: follow רב ענן, but not his reason
steps.stepSummary: A message came from ארץ ישראל: the הלכה follows רב ענן's outcome, but not his reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent from there: The הלכה is like רב ענן, but not because of his reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling sent from ארץ ישראל. It agrees with רב ענן's result but not his reason, and the next steps explain what that means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a split verdict. The husband loses, as רב ענן said. But the reason רב ענן gave, the narrow reading of 'my heirs,' is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: they sent from there (from ארץ ישראל)
but not because of his reason

phrases.english: They sent from there:
The halacha is like Rav Anan,
but not because of his reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between רב הונא and רב ענן
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The husband does not inherit, but not because of how 'my heirs' is read.

steps.title: Which part of רב ענן is accepted: the husband does not inherit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the ruling to explain it. We follow רב ענן in the result: the husband does not inherit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is like רב ענן that the husband does not inherit, but not because of his reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the ruling and starts to explain it. First it states the part we accept: the husband does not inherit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line pins down exactly what 'the הלכה is like רב ענן' covers: only the bottom line. The words 'but not because of his reason' set up the next two steps, which reject his reason and give a new one.

phrases.english: The halacha is like Rav Anan:
that the husband does not inherit,
but not because of his reason;

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב עָנָן דְּבַעַל לָא יָרֵית
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Practical result: the husband gets nothing.

steps.title: Why רב ענן's reason is rejected: a grandson would inherit
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן's reading would mean that even the daughter's son could not inherit. That is wrong. A daughter's son certainly would inherit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן holds that even if his daughter had a son, the son would not inherit. That is not so. If his daughter had a son, he would certainly inherit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why רב ענן's reasoning fails. It points to a case where his reading gives a result everyone rejects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'my heirs' excludes heirs of heirs, then the daughter's son would also be shut out, since he is the heir of an heir. But the ruling from ארץ ישראל says such a son certainly inherits. So the narrow reading of 'my heirs' cannot be the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: a son of his daughter (his grandson)

phrases.english: For Rav Anan holds:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ בְּרָא לִבְרַתֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: even if his daughter had a son,
he would not inherit;
but that is not so,
for if his daughter had a son,
he would certainly inherit;

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב ענן's reasoning, not his ruling about the husband
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His narrow reading would wrongly exclude the daughter's son, who certainly inherits.

steps.title: The real reason: a husband does not inherit ראוי
steps.stepSummary: The husband loses because the property was only ראוי (still due to come) to his wife when she died. A husband does not inherit ראוי the way he inherits מוחזק (what she actually held).
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the reason the husband does not inherit: because it was ראוי to her, and a husband does not take ראוי the way he takes מוחזק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true reason the husband loses. It is a rule about what a husband can inherit from his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife died before the grandmother, so the property never actually came into her hands. It was only on its way to her (ראוי). A husband inherits only what his wife actually owned (מוחזק). A son is different, which is why the grandson in step 6 would inherit.

keyTerms.meaning: property due to come to someone but not yet in hand

steps.whatToRemember: The husband loses. This is not because of how 'my heirs' is read. It is because a husband does not inherit ראוי, property his wife was only due to receive, the way he inherits מוחזק.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'אין הבעל נוטל בראוי כבמוחזק' is a basic rule of inheritance. It shifts the case from a question of wording to a fixed rule of law.

phrases.english: And this is the reason the husband does not inherit:
because it was "due" property,
phrases.notes: His wife died before the grandmother, so the property was only on its way to her and never in her hands.

phrases.english: and a husband does not take what is due as he takes what is held.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the replacement reason after rejecting רב ענן's
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A husband does not inherit ראוי, so he loses this property.

steps.title: Does רב הונא hold that a husband inherits ראוי?
steps.stepSummary: If the true reason is ראוי, then רב הונא, who lets the husband inherit, seems to hold that a husband does take ראוי. The גמרא is surprised by this.
steps.simpleTranslation: By inference, does רב הונא hold that a husband takes ראוי the way he takes מוחזק?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the new reason. It challenges רב הונא, since his view now seems to clash with a known rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 made the case depend on the rule about ראוי. Since רב הונא gave the property to the husband, it looks as if he rejects that rule. The surprised tone shows this sounds hard to accept. The next step answers it.

phrases.english: By inference, does Rav Huna hold:
a husband takes what is due as he takes what is held?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 7's reason back to רב הונא's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the case turns on ראוי, then letting the husband inherit means holding that a husband takes ראוי. That seems to go against the known rule.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר explains רב הונא: 'after you' means 'from now'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר defends רב הונא. Saying 'after you' is like saying 'from now,' so the wife already owned the property, and it counts as מוחזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Great people opened this matter, and small people finished it. Anyone who says 'after you' is like someone who says 'from now.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the surprise from step 8. He shows that רב הונא never said a husband takes ראוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone gives property with the words 'to you, and after you to another,' the second person becomes the owner right now. The first person only gets to use it. So the wife already owned the property in her lifetime. It was מוחזק, and her husband inherits it in the normal way.

keyTerms.meaning: 'After you': a gift that passes to a second person after the first one dies
Opened by great people and finished by small people: a humble way of saying 'I am finishing a great teacher's idea'

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר does not argue with the rule that a husband does not take ראוי. He agrees with that rule. He is saying this property was really מוחזק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
This matter was opened by great people
phrases.notes: The 'great people' means רב הונא. The 'small people' in the next line is רבי אלעזר, humbly talking about himself.

phrases.english: and was finished by small people.
Anyone who says: 'After you,'
phrases.notes: He means someone who gives property and says, 'It is yours, and after you it goes to so-and-so.'

phrases.english: is like one who says: 'From now.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר זֶה נִפְתַּח בִּגְדוֹלִים וְנִסְתַּיֵּים בִּקְטַנִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by showing that רב הונא's case involves מוחזק, not ראוי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the property was already owned by the wife, so it is מוחזק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא lets the husband inherit, so it looked as if he holds that a husband takes ראוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'After you' works like 'from now.' The wife owned the property during her life, so the husband inherits it as מוחזק.

steps.title: רבה supports the view from ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the reasoning of בני מערבא (the property was only ראוי) makes sense. Proof: the older woman could have sold it first, and her sale would have been valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The reasoning of the people of the West makes sense. If the grandmother had sold the property first, her sale would have been a valid sale.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה takes the side of the message from ארץ ישראל and gives a proof for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wife truly owned the property 'from now,' the older woman could not have sold it. But if she sold it, the sale would hold, and the wife would get nothing. That shows the wife did not really own it yet. It was only ראוי to her, which goes against רבי אלעזר's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it is reasonable
'The people of the West': the scholars of ארץ ישראל
The grandmother (the older woman who held the property)
Her sale is a valid sale

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה: מִסְתַּבְּרָא טַעְמָא דִּבְנֵי מַעְרְבָא,
phrases.english: Rabbah said: The reasoning of the people of the West makes sense,
phrases.notes: This is the reasoning from step 7: the husband loses because the property was only ראוי.

phrases.english: because if the grandmother had gone ahead and sold it first,
her sale would be a valid sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes against רבי אלעזר's explanation and supports the ראוי reasoning from ארץ ישראל.
steps.raayaObject: The reasoning of בני מערבא: the property was only ראוי to the wife.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: the older woman's sale would have been valid, so the wife never truly owned the property.

steps.title: רב פפא's final ruling on 'due' property and loans
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules: a husband does not take ראוי the way he takes מוחזק. A בכור does not take a double share in ראוי. A בכור also does not take a double share of a loan, whether it was paid back with land or with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said, the הלכה is: A husband does not take property that was only due, the way he takes property that was held. A בכור does not take a double share of property that was only due, the way he does of property that was held. And a בכור does not take a double share of a loan, whether they collected land or money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the topic with the practical הלכה from רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of ראוי versus מוחזק applies to two people: the husband who inherits his wife, and the בכור who gets a double share. A loan owed to the father counts as ראוי. So the בכור gets no double share of it, even after it is paid back in land.

keyTerms.meaning: Property still due to come, not yet held
A loan owed to the father

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: a husband and a בכור take only from property that was מוחזק, not from property that was ראוי. A loan counts as ראוי for the בכור, whether it is paid back with land or with money.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for inheritance. It decides which property a husband inherits from his wife and which property gives a בכור his double share.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said, the halacha is:
the husband does not take what was due as he takes what was held;
and the firstborn does not take a double share of what was due as he does of what was held.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַבְּכוֹר נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם בַּמִּלְוָה –
phrases.english: And the firstborn does not take a double share of a loan,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁגָּבוּ קַרְקַע, בֵּין שֶׁגָּבוּ מָעוֹת.
phrases.english: whether they collected land or whether they collected money.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the brothers, who collect the debt after their father dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the debate in favor of the ראוי reasoning and extends it to the בכור and to loans.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A husband and a בכור take only from מוחזק, not from ראוי. A בכור gets no double share of a loan, whether it is paid back in land or in money.
